Methods

Ran atomscan and cleave facts against each original. Kept original facts,
scans, fetched bytes and .forage.json records under the named scratch root,
in bad-analysis/. Used bsdtar for the RAR (7-Zip cannot extract this RAR's
method), 7-Zip and binary-refinery xtnsis for the inner NSIS executable,
Capstone and bounded Unicorn CPU-only traces. No sample API, installer or
package install script executed. Compared official registry tarball bytes.

D6F4024132AA: MALICIOUS -- invoice-lured NSIS shellcode loader
------------------------------------------------------------
RAR has one Armenian invoice-named .exe, an NSIS 3 Unicode installer. Its
version strings describe dyrehandlen/fritog.exe, unrelated to an invoice;
its self-issued Lektion Authenticode signature verifies cryptographically.
Self-signing alone does not establish maliciousness. An unsigned System.dll
plug-in finding belongs to the embedded DLL, not to the signed installer.

The decompiled .onMouseOverSection path extracts data under LOCALAPPDATA,
hides its installer window and calls a command reconstruction loop. It seeks
through Namelessless in 473-byte steps from offset 1, appending one character
at each step until H, and passes the reconstructed command to System::Call.
Recovered commands, in execution order:
  kernel32::CreateFileA(... r4 ..., GENERIC_READ, ..., OPEN_ALWAYS, ...)i.r5
  kernel32::SetFilePointer(i r5, i 1084, ...)
  kernel32::VirtualAlloc(i 0,i 45260800,i 0x3000,i 0x40)p.r1
  kernel32::ReadFile(i r5,i r1,i 45260800,*i 0,i 0)i.r3
  user32::EnumWindows(i r1,i 0)
r4 names the extracted Sylvanises member. Thus the returned allocation r1 is
both the ReadFile destination and the native callback. This is a linked
file-to-executable-memory activation chain, not a conclusion from unrelated
API names. Runtime success or a final payload identity is not needed to
establish it. The NSIS callback trigger is preserved; no claim that a merely
opened archive automatically runs the chain is made.

Sylvanises SHA256:
  2d2c3479f1a8b46d19a7efc54bbffb8a74b509d4c36ea35cf6b8bddcf0d85633
Its entry at file offset 1084 traverses valid SIMD blocks and short jumps
across unreachable junk. The reachable code fills a large memory region,
copies a staged range and XORs DWORDs with ESI=0x47f85240, then CALL EAX.
The source range begins at callback-relative 0x1715; requested length is
0x1df8c, extending beyond the file bytes into the zero-filled allocation.
Recovered stage bytes branch over junk, find a page boundary, overwrite an
earlier code range, initialize an obfuscated stack frame, execute a large
RDTSC/counter loop, and reach a PEB/loader-based resolver via FS:[0x30].
The CPU continuation explicitly shortened the counter delay; this is a
conditional trace, not evidence of success in a real Windows process.
No final downloaded payload, exfiltration, persistence or remote injection
is claimed. Additional large opaque embedded files remain unresolved.

Detection additions:
  - Strided NSIS command concealment (suspicious).
  - Repeated SIMD blocks jumping over junk (suspicious).
  - File-to-RWX callback command linkage (notable capability).
  - Concealed callback payload activation (hostile).
These are separate supported observations. Only one distinct hostile outcome
is established; two additional hostile objectives would invent behavior.
This is the evidence-supported gap against the requested hostile-rule count.
The two independent suspicious observations supply the supported minimum.
Added the native-call activation sink to TAXONOMY.md rather than mislabeling
local callback execution as remote process injection or PE image mapping.

New matching is independent of campaign filenames, addresses, allocation size,
XOR key, exact stride and register number. The stride detector checks a table
header in the first KiB, strides 3..1024 and files under 2 MB; the linkage
checks the next 512 decoded characters. These are explicit coverage bounds.
The engine retains only eight YARA pattern matches: conditions walk the
bounded table independently of those evidence offsets, avoiding a missed
command after numerous incidental single-byte matches. SIMD controls check
actual short-jump destinations, not just nearby opcodes.

68D172673D7C: BENIGN -- hosts-file blocking fragment
-------------------------------------------------
All 59 bytes are two hosts entries:
  127.0.0.1 www.gnnloelond.com
  127.0.0.1 go.upupdo.com
There is no script, executable header, macro, autorun directive, trailing
payload or dependency. These records map names to loopback; they neither
contact those hosts nor execute anything. Forager HTTP fetch attempts for
both domains failed DNS resolution. Their present availability does not
prove their historical role. No security-product target or malicious
redirection is established. A security engineer would treat this artifact
as blocking configuration, with its provenance and installation history
unknown. The hostile source label may be an extracted worm-associated file
or a collection mislabel; it does not turn these bytes into a worm.
The accurate loopback-hosts-name-entry finding is unchanged.

5F4E9B028573: BENIGN -- official PostHog browser SDK 1.359.1
---------------------------------------------------------
Forager fetched pkg:npm/posthog-js@1.359.1. Its original npm tarball SHA256 is
identical to the submitted sample, and manifest identity/version agree.
The CommonJS entry loads extension registration and exports init_as_module;
PostHog.init supplies the project token/configuration. Capture collects
configured DOM/usage properties and sends events through request.js using
XHR, fetch or sendBeacon. Default API host is https://us.i.posthog.com.
Persistent identities/cookies, gzip/Base64 event serialization, feature flags,
UI extensions and rrweb session recording fit the documented SDK purpose.
Autocapture explicitly excludes password/hidden fields, sensitive element
classes/names and credit-card/SSN-like values. This is corroborating context,
not a blanket guarantee of privacy or consent in every deployment.

Read the external loader: /static/<kind>.js?v=<SDK version> is loaded from the
configured assets host. Fetched the public documentation and the live
recorder-v2.js response from us-assets.i.posthog.com with the version query;
the response is a recorder implementation. A live version-query response
is not asserted to be an immutable historical release. Fetched and scanned
all 13 direct runtime dependency artifacts at the declared lower bound or
exact pin, including @posthog/core@1.23.2 and @posthog/types@1.359.1, and read
their manifests and representative networking/module code. No dependency
payload inconsistent with its function was identified. The package has no
installed lockfile, so the exact versions of a hypothetical later install
are unknown. No dependencies or lifecycle scripts were executed.

The initial hostile queue label is plausibly driven by privacy-sensitive
analytics/session recording, bot filtering, minified bundles, source maps
and legacy ActiveX compatibility code. These capabilities are retained as
analyst observations; misuse or absent deployment consent is not invented.
All submitted-archive suspicious/hostile findings were investigated: there
were none in the actual firing trait set, despite ambiguous capabilities.

Corrections (no severity reductions):
  1. Cron rule accepted any @word. In product-tours source maps it matched
     JSDoc '* @param root The root ...', not a schedule. Split the numeric
     schedule and the eight standard macro forms into precise notable atoms;
     retained the existing composite ID for objective consumers. Audited its
     two exact consumers and ancestor selectors. The existing traversal cron
     attacks still fire. A transparent umbrella may be stripped when unused;
     the corresponding notable schedule atom preserves the observation.
  2. OpenRead regex crossed names-array entries: 'handleToggleOpen',
     'unreadCount'. Require nearby WebClient context and prevent method-token
     gaps crossing whitespace, quotes or commas. A bare File.OpenRead is a
     filesystem API, not HTTP. Audited the image-LSB extraction consumer and
     broad HTTP-client consumers. Retained an obfuscated WebClient OpenRead
     positive and tested the source-map/filesystem near misses.
  3. The crawler-token composite said 'Forged'. Tokens also occur in blocked
     user-agent lists. Changed its description to an AI crawler reference;
     matcher, ID, scope, criticality and consumers are unchanged.

Verification
------------
24 focused controls pass via:
  python3 testdata/triage/nsis-stride-cron/check.py
They include alternate stride/register/size positives, read/callback register
mismatches, non-RWX allocation, unobfuscated commands, valid SIMD fallthrough,
all eight cron macros, numeric cron, JSDoc, WebClient and source-map near
misses, plus existing JavaScript/Python traversal-to-root-cron attack fixtures
outside this batch and their comment-only negative.

Original RAR/member rescan loses no firing trait and adds the four observations
above; all seven analyzed archive units remain represented. Hosts scan is
unchanged. RAR terminal classification changes BENIGN to HOSTILE; hosts and
PostHog remain BENIGN. No remaining sample/classifier verdict disagreement.
Raw model probabilities are not calibrated verdicts, and the engine warns
that the v18 model does not consume all newer v19 extractor features.

Normalized before/after coverage comparison
------------------------------------------
Rebuilt the original rules from HEAD into scratch and rescanned PostHog with
the identical current engine, explicit --follow=none and validation setting.
This avoids comparing follow-expanded/low-tier diagnostic output with an
artifact-only scan. Across the submitted archive, the only removed trait IDs
are the unsupported OpenRead and root-cron findings described above. No
accurate network, cookie, encoding, execution, telemetry, library or metadata
detection is lost. Neither benign sample gains suspicious/hostile findings.
Normalized model probability changes 0.85152185 -> 0.83623123 for PostHog;
its classifier verdict remains BENIGN. The hosts probability is unchanged.
